title: Development Lifecycle: Plan, Build, Test, Improve
learningObjectives: Define the goal and acceptance criteria.

understand.concept: A development lifecycle is a repeatable, iterative loop: understand a need, plan, build, test, review evidence, and improve. Testing or feedback may send work back to an earlier step; this is not a rigid one-way sequence.
understand.whyItMatters: Clear, repeatable practices help beginners make safe changes and understand how work moves from an idea to a checked result.
understand.analogy: A small checklist helps a person complete a task in order without forgetting important steps.
understand.analogyLimit: Software workflows also involve technical tools, dependencies, collaboration, and test evidence, which a checklist analogy cannot fully describe.

explain.narrative: For a small project, a lightweight checklist is enough: write a goal, make one small change, check expected behavior, review the result, and note what to improve next. Larger projects may use tickets, milestones, automated checks, and release plans.
